## Summary

* Add the initial PlugFn package tree, including TypeScript runtime, client, CLI, providers, docs, examples, tests, Python package, and release/provider gate scripts.
* Add shared package support needed by PlugFn: Hono mount-path handling, OAuth revocation/disconnect improvements, and DB adapter guidance around internal schema wrapping.
* Update FileFn server initialization to wrap incoming database adapters with FileFn schema internally.

## Scope notes

* Excludes `.conduct` artifacts from `plugfn/`, `packages/`, and `filefn/`.
* Preserves the existing `filefn/docs` tree from `origin/dev`.
* Does not include root `package.json` or `package-lock.json` workspace wiring from `next`.

## Validation

* `npm exec -- vitest --run packages/http-hono/src/__tests__/adapter.test.ts packages/oauth-flow/src/__tests__/refresh-disconnect.test.ts packages/oauth-http/tests/token-client.test.ts`
  * `packages/oauth-http/tests/token-client.test.ts` passed: 19 tests.
  * `packages/http-hono` and `packages/oauth-flow` suites did not run because the fresh worktree is missing linked workspace dependencies (`hono`, `@superfunctions/oauth-http`).

---

## Summary by cubic

Adds PlugFn, a shared, self-hosted integration runtime with a TypeScript core, CLI, and browser client, plus updates to HTTP, OAuth, middleware, and DB layers. Implements [SFO-8](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SFO-8/plugfn-init-shared-oauth-primitives) by delivering the initial runtime, tooling, schema, and docs to start building providers and workflows.

* **New Features**
  * `plugfn` core: provider/connection lifecycle, OAuth/webhooks HTTP router, workflows, storage adapters, middleware, policies, and security utilities.
  * `@plugfn/cli`: init, provider scaffolding, type generation, diagnostics, and test utilities.
  * `@plugfn/client`: browser-safe client with OAuth start/disconnect, connection list, and sync APIs.
  * Python shim and initial docs/spec for the public contract.
  * `@superfunctions/http-hono`: mount-path aware `toHono(router, { mountPath })`; 400 if upstream middleware consumed the body; exports `ToHonoOptions`.
  * `@superfunctions/middleware` rate limiter: `checkMany(keys[])` for atomic multi-key checks with a shared reset time.
  * `@superfunctions/oauth-http`: GitHub Apps revocation via `https://api.github.com/applications/{client_id}/token` with `{client_id}` resolution.
  * `@superfunctions/oauth-flow`: disconnect events include upstream revoke error details.
  * DB adapters: deprecate `adapterSchema`; wrap adapters with `wrapWithSchema(adapter, getSchema({ namespace }))`. `filefn` now wraps incoming adapters.
  * Dependency pin: `hono@4.11.9`.
* **Migration**
  * Wrap DB adapters in function init: `wrapWithSchema(adapter, getSchema({ namespace }))`; stop using adapter-level `adapterSchema`.
  * Update GitHub provider `revocationUrl` to `https://api.github.com/applications/{client_id}/token`.
  * When mounting in Hono, use `toHono(router)` and avoid consuming the request body in upstream middleware; pass `{ mountPath }` if needed.

Written for commit 62d3cd010542fe25c687b04932960ae3c51a421a. Summary will update on new commits.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow canonical FastAPI callbacks without provider query**

When clients register the canonical callback URL `/api/plugfn/callback`, OAuth providers redirect back with `code` and `state` but no `provider` query parameter. Because `provider` is a required FastAPI parameter here and is not part of the route path, those real callbacks are rejected with a 422 before `_handle_callback` can use the stored state to identify the provider, so the advertised canonical callback route cannot complete OAuth.

Any app that registers `/api/plugfn/callback` as its redirect URI (the canonical route exposed by the adapter) cannot finish OAuth unless the provider also happens to append a nonstandard `provider` query parameter.

## Comparison between inconvertible types Variable 'value' is of type date, object or regular expression, but it is compared to an expression of type null. --- The best fix is to replace the value !== null check with a truthiness object guard that still excludes null but avoids the specific comparison CodeQL flags.

In plugfn/core/src/core/connection-manager.ts, update isOAuthSecretResolverConfig (around lines 1099–1105):

  • Change:
    • typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && ...
  • To:
    • !!value && typeof value === 'object' && ...

This preserves behavior:

  • null is rejected (!!null is false),
  • non-object truthy primitives are rejected by typeof value === 'object',
  • object values proceed to 'resolveOAuthClient' in value.

No new imports, methods, or dependencies are required.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use latest blocked reset time in checkMany**

When `checkMany` rejects because more than one key is blocked, it computes `resetAt` with `Math.min(...)`, which returns the earliest unblock time among blocked keys. A caller that retries at that timestamp can still be denied by another key whose window resets later, so the returned retry hint is incorrect under mixed per-key states (e.g., token bucket keys drained at different times). Use the latest blocked reset time so `resetAt` represents when the combined check can actually pass.
